story: Gary sits at the architectural review desk in Town Hall, determined to submit his request for parade lights and a sound system on his golf cart. Donna, impatient as ever, is already heading down Magnolia Loop while Hal scans the street with his binoculars for grass parking or stray ornaments. Rosa is also making her way to Magnolia Loop, content to see what the afternoon brings in the humid, hazy heat of 83 degrees.
events: Gary (architectural review desk): Submit cart modification request for parade lights and sound system
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal (hal binoculars): Sweep Magnolia Loop one more time for grass parking or stray ornaments

gary.thought_process: I'm at Town Hall with the cart form already filled out at the signup table. L-01 says exterior cart modifications visible from the street need Architectural Review approval, and my lights and sound system definitely count. The architectural_review_desk is right here, so I should file the request now rather than wait. Lights are fine from Thanksgiving through January 15, and I'll keep the sound off during quiet hours. Getting this done puts me one step closer to the parade, and it's the kind of thing I like to do right.

parameters.content: Submit cart modification request for parade lights and sound system

donna.thought_process: I've been standing at Gary's door for two ticks now and nobody has come out. No one's in line-of-sight, so speaking to him isn't possible from here. I shouldn't keep waiting forever. His house has a workbench, cart, toolbox and fridge, so he may be out back or already gone. The best move is to head back to Magnolia Loop and then on to the courts, or check for him there. I'll go back out to the street to look for him and keep my day moving.

parameters.content: Gary isn't answering, so I'm heading back out to the street to look for him and then on to the courts.

hal.thought_process: I tested the chair last tick and it held up fine. Gary and Donna have squared away their violations, and the notebook entries are closed out. Nobody's on Magnolia Loop, and it's a hazy afternoon. No sense shuffling papers I've already shuffled. Best use of the hour is a quick sweep of the street with the binoculars to confirm all is in order, then settle in until Saturday. Habit, but also a sergeant's duty.

parameters.content: Sweep Magnolia Loop one more time for grass parking or stray ornaments

rosa.thought_process: It's 2:17 PM Wednesday and I've already done the seating, prep, marinade check, and blocked off my shift schedule. Gary, Donna and Hal are all confirmed, so there's nothing left to chase. The one real errand left is the grocery run for Saturday, and my list is already jotted down. I'm alone at home, so no one to talk to. Best use of this hour is to head out to Magnolia Loop and get the shopping done rather than circle back over things I've finished.

parameters.content: Prep and seating are done, so I'm heading out with my grocery list to pick up what I need for Saturday's dinner.

matters.text: Gary Kowalski: Submit cart modification request for parade lights and sound system

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
